extracted.intended_audience: dataset creators, ML practitioners, and data stewards responsible for documenting and publishing datasets
extracted.subtask_description: Produce a comprehensive datasheet that documents a dataset's motivation, composition, collection and preprocessing procedures, intended uses, biases, privacy protections, maintenance, and other contextual information to support safe, transparent, and appropriate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive documentation scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets for datasets establish comprehensive documentation standards for datasets, systematically recording creation methodology, data composition, collection procedures, preprocessing transformations, intended applications, potential biases, privacy considerations, and maintenance protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The datasheet should cover the full data lifecycle from collection to disposal and include all elements listed. Purpose: enhance transparency, enable informed decisions about dataset suitability, support bias detection/mitigation, ensure compliance with data protection, and promote responsible stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the motivation for creating the dataset and the problem(s) it is intended to address ("motivation").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the dataset was created, who commissioned it, and the intended target tasks or research questions. This helps consumers judge relevance and appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition and characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Record what the dataset contains and its key characteristics (e.g., "statistical distributions, temporal coverage, and known quality characteristics").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include counts, class balances, demographic breakdowns, file/formats, sampling frames, and summary statistics. Provide examples or representative samples where appropriate to help consumers evaluate coverage and biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection procedures and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how data were collected, including instruments and procedures (e.g., "sensor calibration procedures, environmental conditions during collection"), sources, and provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document collection dates, locations, personnel, instrumentation/calibration, data acquisition settings, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and any steps taken to ensure data quality and representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing, cleaning, and transformation history
rubrics_metrics.description: Document preprocessing transformations applied to the raw data ("preprocessing transformations").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify cleaning steps, normalization, filtering, augmentation, labeling procedures, imputation, and code or scripts used. Version-control these transformations and provide links or references to reproducible pipelines or repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended uses and recommended applications
rubrics_metrics.description: State recommended uses and intended applications for the dataset ("intended applications", "recommended uses").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list suitable tasks and warning against known misuse or inappropriate applications. Map research questions to suggested analyses when applicable (see DAIMS example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Known limitations and distributional gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Document known limitations, distributional gaps, and scenarios the dataset does not cover ("known distributional gaps", "limitations").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about where the dataset is weak or likely to fail (temporal/geographic/demographic gaps, edge cases). This supports safety assessment and helps consumers avoid inappropriate deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias and fairness considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record potential biases and demographic representation information to support fairness assessment (e.g., "demographic representation across different job categories").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide demographic breakdowns, labeler protocols, known sources of bias, and advice for bias detection/mitigation. Indicate whether and how sensitive attributes were collected or inferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy, consent, and data-sharing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Document privacy protections, anonymisation procedures, participant consent, and any data sharing constraints ("patient privacy protections, anonymisation procedures, and data sharing constraints").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe consent processes, de-identification techniques, differential privacy or other mitigation measures, legal/regulatory constraints, and restrictions on redistribution or re-identification risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance, versioning, and update practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe maintenance protocols and practices for keeping documentation and the dataset up to date ("maintenance protocols", "ongoing maintenance to ensure documentation accuracy").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include versioning strategy, update frequency, changelogs, responsible contacts, and processes for deprecation or disposal. Recommend using tools like Data Version Control (DVC) and audit trails to track evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability, monitoring, and suitability for production
rubrics_metrics.description: Document properties that support operational reliability ("support model monitoring pipelines, detect data drift, assess whether production data remains within the documented training distribution").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide baselines and metrics that monitoring systems can use (e.g., distributions, thresholds). Note how dataset statistics should be monitored in prod and guidance for retraining decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety-critical documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For safety-critical datasets, include records relevant to safety assessments ("sensor calibration procedures, environmental conditions during collection, edge-case scenario coverage").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide extra detail on edge-case coverage, environmental/operational conditions, test results, and any known failure modes to support regulatory submissions and safety engineering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of complementary documentation and tooling
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend complementary techniques such as Model Cards, Data Version Control, and Model Development Audit Trails to augment the datasheet ("Related Techniques: Model Cards; Data Version Control; Model Development Audit Trails").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to or include model cards for downstream models, use DVC for reproducible data/transform tracking, and maintain audit trails to document decisions and changes for accountability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation costs, practicality, and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge practical limitations of producing datasheets ("requires significant time investment and domain expertise", "information may become outdated", "absence of standardised templates and enforcement mechanisms").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document trade-offs, resource needs, and any incomplete areas in the datasheet. Encourage automation and tool integration (as DAIMS does) to reduce burden and prioritize critical fields for release if resources are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of incomplete or misleading documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about risks such as intentional omission of sensitive information and limited adoption leading to inconsistent documentation quality ("dataset creators may intentionally omit sensitive information", "limited adoption and awareness").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparency statements about omitted fields and rationale, and include contact/verification mechanisms. Encourage community standards and repositories to improve consistency and discoverability.
